title: INC Ransom
summary: INC Ransom is a ransomware operation that public reporting tracks from 2023, and it follows the double extortion model: copy data, encrypt, then publish when payment does not arrive. Reporting describes targeting that skews toward healthcare, education, and local government, sectors where downtime is expensive and where stolen patient or citizen records add pressure. Analysts have observed the operation using legitimate remote management tools alongside commodity intrusion utilities, plus encryptors that reach both Windows hosts and virtualisation servers. The public brand has also been imitated by other criminals, so a matching note or family name does not prove that the same operator is responsible, and shared indicators have limited value when scoping an incident. Evidence is behavioural: new administrative accounts, service installations, mass archive creation, unusually large outbound transfers, and disablement of endpoint protection before encryption. Attribution to any earlier group is reported with limited confidence.

beginner.definition: INC Ransom is the name of a criminal group that attacks companies with ransomware. Ransomware is software that locks files and asks for money to unlock them. This group also steals data first, and it threatens to publish that data. Public reports say it often targets hospitals, schools, and local government offices.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hospitals cannot wait for files to be restored. When patient records are locked, care itself is at risk. This group chooses targets where the pressure is highest, so a quick payment seems tempting. But paying does not remove the stolen data, and it funds the next attack. Good backups and fast detection are the only reliable answers.
howItWorks: The group gains a first way into a network, often by using stolen passwords.
It looks for servers that hold many important files, such as patient records.
Before locking anything, the group copies those files out to its own storage.
Then it runs an encrypting program, which scrambles files and adds new endings.
Staff find that shared folders no longer open, and a note appears on screens.
The group then threatens to publish the stolen data if the victim does not pay.
beginner.example: Imagine a small clinic where every paper file is kept in one room. A thief breaks in, photographs all the files, and then jams the door locks. He leaves a note saying he will publish the photographs unless the clinic pays. Repairing the locks takes weeks, and the photographs already exist. Even if the clinic pays, it can never be sure the copies are gone. That is why the theft, not only the locked door, is the real problem.
takeaways: Treat stolen data and locked files as two separate problems.
Test your backups by restoring them, not only by taking them.
Watch for new administration tools appearing on servers.

objectives: Explain what INC Ransom is and why healthcare and public sector targets are attractive.
Describe the sequence from initial access to encryption and publication threats.
Explain why an imitated ransomware brand weakens indicator-based scoping.
Identify the behavioural evidence that precedes encryption on a corporate network.
Summarise the backup and recovery tests that reduce dependence on a payment decision.
Describe how to state attribution for a criminal operation using limited confidence language.
